html:
SMTO-CAP-0009 — Your capability settings name a Skill or tool that isn't installed

GUID: 9da939bb-f7ca-47e4-a2b6-e8a0057b5c79
Slug: capability-reference-unknown
Domain: CAP · Subsystem: cap

What happened

  • Your saved capability choices mention a Skill or tool this SMTO doesn't have, often because it was removed or renamed. SMTO won't use a choice it can't match, so it didn't accept them.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Capabilities by the message box, select Refresh catalog, and note the name the message says is unknown. Refreshing loads the Skills and tools that are installed right now, so you can see what is missing.
  2. If you still need that Skill, select Manage user skills (the User Skills page) and install it again, or select Enable if it shows Disabled. Once the Skill is back, your saved choice matches it again.
  3. If you don't need it, select Use inherited capabilities (or Reset to product default for Global), then set your other choices again and select Apply. Clearing that scope's rules removes the reference to the missing item.

What success looks like

  • Apply closes the Capabilities window without an error, and your next request starts normally.

If it still fails

  • Send Copy error details to the person who manages SMTO; they name the missing Skill or tool. Don't try similar names until one is accepted; pick the exact item shown in the refreshed list.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • normalize_policy rejected the capability policy because an enabled, preferred or excluded skill_ids or tool_ids entry is not present in the current registry (Unknown canonical skill_ids/tool_ids).

What this means

  • A policy preference or exclusion names an identity absent from the current canonical tool/skill registry. Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.

Why this can happen

  • A policy preference or exclusion names an identity absent from the current canonical tool/skill registry.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the named ID with the installed registry, checking whether an integration was removed or renamed.

How to fix it

  • Compare the listed IDs with registry.skill_policy_metadata() and registry.tool_ids() (normalize_policy in src/agent_runtime/capability_policy.py). Restore or re-enable the removed or renamed Skill on /skills, or remove the stale IDs from the prompt, conversation or global policy (PUT /api/agent/capabilities/settings/global or the conversation capability-settings endpoint).
  • Refresh the capability list and select an exact registered identity. If a required skill is missing, restore that installation first.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Every policy identity resolves in the current registry before the policy is accepted.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
